pages.note: Both render the conclusion of the four past-self views, the extension to the future views (MMK 27.13) and the start of the 'world is permanent' refutation (lha de mi de na) correctly; A adds the first two past views to the list before saying 'the latter two', where the Tibetan names only the two (gnyi ga / gnyi ga ma yin), and it finishes the page-final sentence fragment with 'leads to'; both are harmless and not serious.

Both keep the speakers right through this passage: the opponent's question, the root verse 'lha ni ma skyes nyid 'gyur te / rtag la skye ba med phyir ro', the opponent's claim of one permanent self, the commentator's 'de ni bzang po ma yin te' reply, and the 'gzhan nyid' horn (lha las mi gzhan na ... mi rtag 'gyur'); the word read as skyes pa kho nas in line 3 is hard to make out on the image.

Both translate the Devadatta/Yajnadatta continuum argument, the opponent's dilemma (gtan tshigs ma grub / dpe ma grub, split by different vs non-different continua), the reply 'gtan tshigs spyir brjod pa'i phyir skyon med do', and the verse 'gal te phyogs gcig lha yin la' faithfully; they differ only in wording.
